'''Okaro Wayne Anthony White'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Okaro Wayne Anthony White () - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/212547-okaro-wayne-anthony-white |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=26 July 2025}}</ref> (born August 13, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who most recently played for [[BC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] of the [[VTB United League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]] and went on to play three season in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

With Florida State, White was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Defensive Team during his senior season. He went undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]] and made his NBA debut with the [[Miami Heat]] in 2017. Despite never appearing in a game for them, White was part of the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] team that reached the [[2018 NBA Finals]].

==Early life==
White was born in [[Brooklyn, New York]], on August 13, 1992, and has an older brother and sister. His mother, Charmaine White, ran [[track and field|track]] for the Jamaica national team. As a preteen, his family moved to [[Clearwater, Florida]], to be close to his grandmother.{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

In eighth grade, he experienced a growth spurt, growing five-and-a-half inches in the summer.{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

White was named [[Pinellas County]]'s Basketball Player of the Year as a senior at [[Clearwater High School]].<ref name=playerfeature>{{cite web|last1=Holub|first1=Bonnie|title=Player Feature: Okaro White|url=http://www.seminoles.com/fls/32900/old_site/pdf/m-baskbl/2013-14/misc_non_event/okaro-white-opens-up.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=32900|website=[[Florida State Seminoles]]|publisher=[[Florida State University]]|access-date=June 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303220846/https://seminoles.com/fls/32900/old_site/pdf/m-baskbl/2013-14/misc_non_event/okaro-white-opens-up.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=32900 |archive-date=March 3, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
White chose to play college basketball at [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] after receiving scholarship offers from [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], and [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Fl.)]]. At Florida State, he started on two NCAA Tournament teams.<ref name=playerfeature/> He averaged 13.6 points and 6.8 rebounds per game in his senior season with Florida State, both career highs. In addition, White connected on 37.5 percent of his 3-point shots. He defended both guards and forwards and alternated between the small and power forward positions.<ref name=palmbeach>{{cite news|last1=Pierre|first1=Natalie|title=FSU's Okaro White, UF's Patric Young lead state NBA draft hopefuls|url=http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/sports/fsus-okaro-white-ufs-patric-young-lead-state-nba-d/ngSL4/|access-date=June 25, 2015|work=[[Palm Beach Post]]|archive-date=July 2, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140702070614/http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/sports/fsus-okaro-white-ufs-patric-young-lead-state-nba-d/ngSL4/|date=June 25, 2014}}</ref> White was one of 64 seniors selected to play in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Putnam|first1=Bob|title=Florida State's Okaro White preps for shot at NBA draft|url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/basketball/nba/florida-states-okaro-white-preps-for-shot-at-nba-draft/2185787/|access-date=June 23, 2015|work=[[Tampa Bay Times]]|date=June 24, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Virtus Bologna (2014–2015)===
After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], White joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]]. In five games, he averaged 8.2 points and 2.6 rebounds per game.<ref name=democrat>{{cite news|last1=Pierre|first1=Natalie|title=Florida State's Okaro White earns invite to Grizzlies training camp|url=http://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2014/07/12/okaro-white-florida-state-miller/12574267/|access-date=June 23, 2015|work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]|date=July 12, 2014}}</ref> On July 31, 2014, he signed with [[Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna|Virtus Bologna]] of Italy for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/129698/virtus-bologna-lands-rookie-okaro-white.html|title=Virtus Bologna lands rookie Okaro White|work=Sportando.com|date=July 31, 2014|access-date=July 15, 2016}}</ref> In 33 games for the club, he averaged 12.1 points, 6.8 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.0 blocks per game in the top-tier [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]].<ref>[http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=WHI-OKA-92 Okaro White|#1.]</ref>

===Aris Thessaloniki (2015–2016)===
In July 2015, White joined the Memphis Grizzlies for the Orlando Summer League and the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the Las Vegas Summer League. On August 7, 2015, he signed a one-year deal with [[Aris B.C.|Aris Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150811021042/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/6987onwhcxxyri8x/aris-brings-in-power-forward-white Aris brings in power forward White]</ref><ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/172014/okaro-white-inks-with-aris-thessaloniki.html Okaro White inks with Aris Thessaloniki]</ref> In 26 Greek League regular season games, he averaged 13.5 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.7 steals, and 0.4 blocks per game.<ref name="greek=profile">[http://esake.gr/el/action/EsakeplayerView?idplayer=68F03044&mode=1&idteam=00000005&idchampionship=38100B0B ΟΥΑΪΤ Οκάρο | Basket League ΣΚΡΑΤΣ 2015–16] {{in lang|el}}</ref> He led the Greek League's regular season phase with a total accumulated [[Performance Index Rating|Performance Index Rating (PIR)]] of 474,<ref>[http://esake.gr/el/action/EsakeStats?mode=2&idchampionship=38100B0B&idseason=00000001&asc=false&sortby=totalrank ΣΥΝΟΛΙΚΑ ΣΤΑΤΙΣΤΙΚΑ ΠΑΙΚΤΩΝ] {{in lang|el}}</ref> thus being the league's regular season [[Greek Basket League statistical leaders#Performance Index Rating leaders (since the 1993–94 season)|PIR leader]].

In 10 Greek League playoff games, he averaged 14.9 points, 8.1 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game.<ref name="greek=profile" /> Over 36 games in [[2015–16 Greek Basket League|2015–16]], he averaged 13.9 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.6 steals per game. He was named to the 2015–16 [[Greek Basket League Pentad|Greek League Best Five]],<ref>[http://www.eurohoops.net/heba/275824/the-all-greek-basket-league-team-of-20152016 The All-Greek Basket League team of 2015/2016]</ref> and he was named the 2015–16 [[Greek Basket League Most Spectacular Player|Greek League Most Spectacular Player]].<ref>[http://www.esake.gr/el/0A3FA6C9 Ο Ο. Γουάιτ πιο θεαματικός παίκτης της Basket League ΣΚΡΑΤΣ] {{in lang|el}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sport24.gr/Basket/ElladaBasket/A1Basket/vraveuontai-oi-kaluteroi-sthn-klhrwsh-ths-basket-league.4248734.html |title=Βραβεύονται οι καλύτεροι στην κλήρωση της Basket League . |access-date=September 6, 2016 |language=el |archive-date=October 11, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011121726/http://www.sport24.gr/Basket/ElladaBasket/A1Basket/vraveuontai-oi-kaluteroi-sthn-klhrwsh-ths-basket-league.4248734.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the [[2015–16 Eurocup Basketball|2015–16 EuroCup season]], he averaged 11.0 points and 6.4 rebounds in 16 games.<ref>[https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/players/?seasoncode=U2015&pcode=006336 WHITE, OKARO – Eurocupbasketball.com]</ref>

===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2016–2017)===
In June 2016, White joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-announce-summer-league-information-1/|title=HEAT Announce Summer League Information|work=NBA.com|date=June 29, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref> He went on to sign with the Heat on July 15, 2016,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-okaro-white|title=HEAT Signs Okaro White|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}}</ref> but he was waived on October 22, after appearing in six preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waives-five-players|title=HEAT Waives Five Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref> On November 1, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Heat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://siouxfalls.dleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announce-2016-training-camp-roster/|title=Skyforce Announce 2016 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2016|access-date=November 3, 2016|archive-date=November 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104075937/http://siouxfalls.dleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announce-2016-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2017–2018)===
On January 17, 2017, he returned to the Heat,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-okaro-white-0|title=HEAT Signs Okaro White|work=NBA.com|date=January 17, 2017|access-date=January 17, 2017}}</ref> signing a 10-day contract with the team<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/IraHeatBeat/status/821395974379700224|title=White has been signed to a 10-day contract. He...|work=Twitter|date=January 17, 2017|access-date=January 17, 2017}}</ref> to help them deal with numerous injuries. Miami had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, being one player over the allowed limited of 15. He made his NBA debut two days later, recording one rebound in nine minutes off the bench in a 99–95 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400900058|title=Mavericks vs. Heat – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=January 19, 2017|access-date=January 19, 2017}}</ref> He signed a second 10-day contract with the Heat on January 27,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-signs-okaro-white-second-10-day-contract|title=HEAT Signs Okaro White to a Second 10-day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 27, 2017|access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref> and a rest-of-season deal on February 6.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-re-signs-okaro-white|title=HEAT RE-SIGNS OKARO WHITE|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2017|access-date=February 6, 2017}}</ref> On February 16, 2017, he was assigned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] so he could participate in the NBA Development League All-Star game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/white-and-georges-hunt-play-nba-development-league-all-star-game|title=White And Georges-Hunt To Play In NBA Development League All-Star Game|work=NBA.com|date=February 16, 2017|access-date=February 22, 2017}}</ref>

On February 8, 2018, the Heat traded White to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Luke Babbitt]] and was later waived.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Trade Babbitt To Heat For Okaro White|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-trade-babbitt-heat-okaro-white|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 8, 2018|date=February 8, 2018}}</ref>

On March 18, 2018, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] signed White to a 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cavs Sign Okaro White To 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/white-10-day-180318|date=March 18, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 18, 2018}}</ref>

On April 7, 2018, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] signed White for the remainder of the season<ref>{{cite news|title=Cavaliers Sign Okaro White for Remainder of Season|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/okaro-white-signed-180407|date=April 7, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 7, 2018}}</ref> and was eligible to play in the playoffs. The Cavaliers made it to the [[2018 NBA Finals]], but lost in four games to the [[Golden State Warriors]].

On August 5, 2018, White was waived by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Waive Okaro White|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/waive-okaro-white-180805|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 5, 2018|date=August 5, 2018}}</ref> On September 24, 2018, White was included in the training camp roster for the [[San Antonio Spurs]]<ref>{{cite web|title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2018–19 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2018-19-training-camp-roster|date=September 24, 2018|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 24, 2018}}</ref> but was later waived by the Spurs on October 13.<ref>{{cite news|title=SPURS WAIVE NICK JOHNSON AND OKARO WHITE|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-waive-nick-johnson-and-okaro-white|date=October 13, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 13, 2018}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2018)===
On November 23, 2018, the [[Washington Wizards]] announced that they had signed White,<ref>{{cite news|title=Wizards sign Okaro White|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-okaro-white|date=November 23, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 23, 2018}}</ref> but White was later waived by the Wizards on December 20.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards sign Ron Baker|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-ron-baker|date=December 20, 2018|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 20, 2018}}</ref>

===Long Island Nets (2019)===
On January 4, 2019, the [[Long Island Nets]] announced that they had acquired White.<ref>{{cite news|title=Long Island Nets Acquire Okaro White|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-acquire-okaro-white|date=January 4, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 4, 2019}}</ref>

===Unics Kazan (2020–2021)===
On August 31, 2020, he signed with [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/okaro-white-joins-unics-kazan/|title=Okaro White joins Unics Kazan|date=August 31, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 31, 2020}}</ref> He reached the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] finals with the Russian club, averaging 10.1 points and 5.4 rebounds per game.{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

===Panathinaikos (2021–2022)===
On July 14, 2021, White officially signed a two-year (1+1) deal with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]], returning to Greece under his [[BC UNICS|Kazan]] coach [[Dimitris Priftis]].<ref>[https://sportando.basketball/en/okaro-white-officialy-signs-with-panathinaikos/ Okaro White {{sic|nolink=y|reason=error in source|offi|cialy}} signs with Panathinaikos]</ref> In 32 [[Greek Basket League]] games, he averaged 11.5 points and 5.3 rebounds, playing around 23 minutes per contest. Additionally, in 29 [[EuroLeague]] games, he averaged 8.4 points and 3.7 rebounds, playing around 23 minutes per contest.{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

===Windy City Bulls (2022)===
On October 23, 2022, White joined the [[Windy City Bulls]] training camp roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ontapsportsnet.com/bulls/windy-city-bulls-training-camp-roster-released-chicago-bulls-two-way-players|website=ontapsportsnet.com|title=Windy City Bulls Finalize Training Camp Roster|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}}</ref>
